legend: Cell block from a patient with HIV and a malignant pleural effusion. The cells have a plasmablastic/immunoblastic appearance with abundant amphophilic cytoplasm.
Cell block from the pleural fluid of an 86-year-old patient with primary effusion lymphoma. The infiltrate includes Reed–Sternberg–like cells with prominent nucleoli.

Biopsy of a jejunal mass from a 38-year-old man with HIV, Kaposi sarcoma, and a circumferential mass in the small bowel (<<29303>>). Cells are positive for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) by in situ hybridization (not shown) and for KSHV/HHV8 latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA) (<<29304>>).

Lymph node with partial involvement by extracavitary primary effusion lymphoma (<<29305>>). Malignant cells show strong nuclear staining for KSHV/HHV8 latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA) (<<29308>>). The cells are positive for CD138, highlighting preferential localization in the lymph node sinus (<<29309>>). Aberrant expression of the T-cell marker CD3 can be seen (<<29306>>).
